title: Coordinator: select the node dir that actually contains chrome-devtools-mcp 1.6.0
description: render_native_schedule.node22_bins() returns every nvm node 22 bin dir (v22.22.0 first, then v22.23.1) and dot-coordinator/scripts/ping-dots.py takes bins[0] unconditionally. On jeff-ubuntu the pinned MCP was installed only under v22.23.1, so the launcher failed closed with 'system Chrome, pinned Chrome DevTools MCP 1.6, or Pi is unavailable' even though Chrome, pi and the MCP were all present. Worked around on 2026-10-21 by npm i -g chrome-devtools-mcp@1.6.0 under v22.22.0, which proves the coordinator send path works on Linux. Root fix: pick the first node dir whose lib/node_modules/chrome-devtools-mcp/build/src/bin/chrome-devtools-mcp.js exists and reports version 1.6.0, else fail with the exact paths searched.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #552 (merged 2de7a13d): pinned_mcp() walks CHROME_DEVTOOLS_MCP_JS then every Node 22 tree and returns the first entrypoint whose package.json reports 1.6.0, failing closed with the searched path list; regressions restored and green on main.

title: PRW human steering: branch matching can credit the wrong PR (reused branches, cache aliases, lifetimes)
description:
Source: Dot reviews of PR #847 rounds 3-7 (heads e7748601, 0e7495ed, f3c73701, d7726f0b; 2026-11-16), receipts pr847-r3..r7-dot.reply.only.txt (review scratch) and gist 6b1ff1cd6a7f044a94b16f00547c1d02. Reproduced on main for correctly-cased events; #847 was narrowed to explicit PR ids so as not to widen these.
Branch matching in aggregate_native_human_steering (scripts/prw_metrics.py) can credit the wrong PR:
1. A verified prompt carrying the exact head SHA of a PR closed before the window is credited to the successor PR that reused the branch (the closed PR leaves the branch index, so the time match wins). Fix: veto weaker matches when the commit is a listed out-of-window head on the same repo/branch.
2. The PR list (from _merge_pr_branch_metadata) keeps lookup-cache alias fields (head_branch, head_sha, created_at_utc, closed_at_utc, merged_at_utc) for cache-only rows; the aggregator reads only headRefName/headRefOid/createdAt/closedAt, so those rows can neither match nor veto. Merging by case-insensitive (repo, number) with live lifecycle precedence must come first, or reading aliases revives stale cache copies (Dot r7 P0).
3. exact_head matching searches all candidates in the report window, ignoring the PR lifetime, so a cached PR created after the prompt can win as BRANCH_HEAD_MATCH (Dot r7 P0 #2).
4. Mixed repository casing between event and PR list makes branch matching miss (miss, not false bind).
5. _sha_matches prefix semantics not used in exact_head (Hermes r7 P2).
Acceptance: each scenario has an aggregator test; no false bind in any; drafted fixes exist on branch fix/prw-binding-repo-case-20261116 history (commits a66bad15..d7726f0b) as a starting point.

title: install-claude-commands.sh silently replaces symlinked skill directories with frozen copies (PR 424)
description:
install-claude-commands.sh:329 install_component runs rm -f on any symlinked intermediate directory under a component target and replaces it with a real copy, with no log line or warning. This PR (424, merged a13dea1b9ef) added a preflight check for this exact condition under scripts/ but not under skills/, so the two paths are handled inconsistently (preflight_history_helper aborts, install_component silently replaces).

Live impact: ~/.claude/skills/dark-factory is a symlink into an actively-edited dark-factory checkout. After one --merge install, that symlink is replaced by a frozen copy; future edits to the dark-factory repo stop reaching ~/.claude with no signal to the user. tests/test_installer.py:724 pins the replace-symlink behavior as intended but never asserts a warning is emitted.

Reproduced in a sandboxed fake HOME: a skills/dark-factory symlink to an external checkout came back as a real directory after --merge (exit 0, no warning), and a sibling file that existed only behind the link was gone.

Fix: either warn loudly, or abort matching the scripts preflight policy, when install_component finds a symlinked target directory, or add an explicit preserve-symlinks opt in or out flag.

Source: /p max review of PR 424 (merged a13dea1b9ef), reproduced with a temp HOME sandbox.

title: Paginate open PR query for stacked PR ceiling
description:
Provenance: PRW-716 independent source review of jleechanorg/jleechan-skills PR #506 at published head `023da1dfe8018f25901bbfaf7f32ad8cb0d05a5e`; official GitHub CLI contract: https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr_list.

Finding (P1, nonblocking): `gh pr list --limit 100` caps the returned open PR rows. A repository with more than 100 open PRs could have at least 9 stacked PRs after the first 100 main-base rows; the hook would see none of them and allow another stacked PR, despite the existing repo-wide `<10` policy. This is a reachable scenario derived from the CLI limit and source path, not an observed live failure in this repository (the current list has 27 open PRs).

Acceptance: count the full open PR set (or otherwise account for pagination) before enforcing the existing stacked cap; add deterministic coverage with more than 100 main-base rows followed by 9 stacked rows; keep existing thresholds and fail-open behavior unchanged. Do not create a new cap.

title: EPIC: ideal skill superset — reconcile 48 divergent skills (repo vs Mac live)
description:
Goal: jleechan-skills contains the IDEAL SUPERSET for every skill — every valid line from both the repo and Mac live, with nothing stale and nothing duplicated. Then install on Mac and jeff-ubuntu.

MEASURED 2026-11-01 against origin/main 8795171eb and ~/.claude/skills:
- 48 skills diverge (excluding 6 explained by shared/retain-local.json)
- 724 repo-only lines + 574 live-only lines = ~1298 line changes
- Buckets: 5 live-superset, 3 repo-newer, 40 mixed, 0 wrap-only, 0 stale-path

DIRECTION RULE: repo is the only source; live is never a source. So every change is made IN THE REPO, reviewed, merged, and only then propagated repo->live. A live-only section is ported INTO the repo by writing it as a proper repo change.

WHY NOT JUST RUN --merge: a blanket install would drop the live-only sections from the live path. A merge backup preserves bytes but the active skill loses them.

SLICES (each its own PR, reviewed independently):
- S1 recover live-only knowledge (5 skills: cmux-goal, repro, repro-evidence, scratch-space, wiki-ingest)
- S2 drive live from repo, repo-newer (3 skills: end2end-testing, harness-engineering, hermes)
- S3 reconcile the 40 mixed skills

DONE WHEN: all 48 have a decided disposition (ported, retained-locally, or confirmed identical), main is the superset, and both hosts verify to the same digest per skill.

title: S1: recover live-only knowledge into the repo (5 skills)
description:
Recover sections that exist ONLY on Mac live and would be lost by any clean install. Each is real operational knowledge, except wiki-ingest which is a defect.

1. cmux-goal (+1 line): 'Probe every clause against every target before setting the goal' - Stop hook reads the condition literally, so unsatisfiable clauses loop to deadline. Cites 2026-05-15 merge-approval loop and 2026-10-30 'CI green' on a repo with no CI. Includes a verified statusCheckRollup probe command and the rule that a commit status an agent posts itself is not CI.
2. repro (+9): '## 0. Repo-level skill first - always' and '## 0.1 Default comparison: original/control/candidate'. Repo has NEITHER section.
3. repro-evidence (+20): same 'Repo-level skill first' plus the full Original/Control/Candidate arm table with provenance rules (original = read-only lookup of the real record, never re-run; n>=5 per arm for stochastic systems).
4. scratch-space (+21): '## Enforcement - /tmp workspace creation is blocked' documenting the live PreToolUse guard, incidents jleechan-zsq5 / jleechan-bu9r, the allowed file-type list, and SCRATCH_GUARD_ALLOW_TMP=1.
5. wiki-ingest (+24): NOT knowledge - 'Phase 9: Commit and Push' is duplicated verbatim (live:2, repo:0). Fix = confirm repo has one Phase 9, do not port the duplicate.

ACCEPTANCE: repo contains each valid section exactly once; no duplicated headings; full test suite green; live synced afterwards.

title: [P1] PR #608: mark truncated replies incomplete in coverage footer
description:

- Add a deterministic oversized-single-entry test at the comment-size boundary asserting the posted body, footer, and downstream coverage result agree that the response is incomplete.

title: Accept valid zero-byte files in authoritative evidence manifests
description:
Provenance: PR #608 exact head `550a64f24430eb8cd21a8c974d44b7a0cac27122`. The direct test receipt correctly records `tests-direct.stderr` as an empty raw capture (size 0 bytes, SHA-256 `e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855`) because pytest wrote no stderr. The manifest builder preserves that file and size, but the shared `web_advice_transport.py::_file_manifest_map` at `~/.claude/skills/web-advice/scripts/web_advice_transport.py:268-270` rejects `size_bytes <= 0` and raises `ReviewPacketIncompleteError`. The current packet-adapter attempt consequently failed on the valid `tests-direct.stderr` entry. The 550a evidence remains valid; root used a separate lossless serialization for publication, so this is a nonblocking adapter follow-up, not a reason to alter the source PR.

Acceptance:
- Accept a zero-byte file manifest entry when its path is valid and its SHA-256 is valid and matches the empty file.
- Continue rejecting negative, non-integer, malformed, or mismatched size/hash metadata.
- Add a regression that calls `assert_review_packet_complete` with an empty stderr artifact and otherwise exact manifests; it passes for size 0 and still fails for a mismatched digest or negative size.
- Verify `build_review_packets.py` emits the empty file as a valid entry and does not omit it.
acceptance_criteria: Allow exact manifest entries for legitimate zero-byte files such as empty stderr; retain strict validation for negative/non-integer sizes, invalid hashes, and mismatches; add assertions for both accepted and rejected cases.

Nonblocking reviewer findings left open on jleechanorg/jleechan-skills PR #833 (self-review fallback), reviewed at d1084835bae91798f880ddb8baab83e15282f76f. Both round-5 reviewers approved; none of these blocks merge. Fix together in one follow-up wording PR.

1. pr-lifecycle/review-recovery.md:28 — "never a standing approval or an earlier one" is stricter than the governing merge rule, pr-lifecycle/SKILL.md:119 ("neither requires nor waives") and pr-workflow-manager/SKILL.md:31 (accepts a standing approval whose conditions apply). Flagged by both reviewers (P1 static, P2 CLI). Either state it as an added restriction for the fallback case, or narrow it to approvals conditioned on /advice approval.
2. review-recovery.md:28 — unclear whether the driver itself may run a merge the user approves while the PR is short of FINAL_READY (SKILL.md:62 and pr-workflow-manager/SKILL.md:31 merge only after FINAL_READY).
3. advice/reviewer-selection.md:76-90 — items 1-4 of the order of attempts are all tier 1; the text does not say whether Dot waits for other hosts' CLI seats; line 96 reads sequentially.
4. review-recovery.md:19,25 vs :9,:13 — the mandatory two-vote /advice substitution for a timed-out Dot or /wa leg is not covered by the fallback, so that PR can still stall.
5. reviewer-selection.md:66-68,79 with review-recovery.md:19 — transient skip reasons (profile/resource contention, exhausted dispatch budget) can qualify a seat and start the fallback early.
6. pr-lifecycle/SKILL.md:93 and six-stage.md:38 say the fallback "satisfies" the gate while review-recovery.md:24 keeps the ledger row OPEN; use one phrase everywhere.
7. review-recovery.md:3 — the file's "load when" line does not mention the self-review fallback.
8. review-records.md:14 — ledger statuses for "Source review quorum" still list only PASS / OPEN; the SELF-REVIEW FALLBACK note is not described there.

Acceptance: one Markdown-only PR resolving 1-8, two independent full-scope reviews at its head (review-policy change), contract-tests green.

title: Coordinator blocks forever on a stale Chrome SingletonLock after a killed tick
description: Repro 2026-10-23 21:20 PDT on the Mac: a coordinator tick for account test wrote ~/.config/dot-headless-chrome-test/SingletonLock -> jeffreys-macbook-pro.local-55981 and did not clean it on exit (PID 55981 was already dead). The next two launcher runs aborted instantly with 'Dot coordinator blocked: Chrome or a stale SingletonLock already owns this Dot profile', even though pgrep showed no Chrome on that profile. Removing SingletonLock/SingletonCookie/SingletonSocket by hand let the run proceed and it delivered normally. dot_chrome.mjs already has waitAndCleanSingletonLock for its own path, and the launcher deliberately kept Chrome's singleton check when the profile flock was deleted, so it should clean a PROVABLY stale lock (holder PID in the symlink target is not alive) and keep blocking only for a live holder. Minimum patch: parse the trailing PID from the SingletonLock target, and when that PID is dead remove the three singleton files before the existing checks. Blocker for implementing now: coordinator launch glue is at 149 of the 150 LOC cap, so this needs either ~8 lines of headroom (operator cap decision) or code moved by agreement.

comments.author: pi
comments.text: WITHDRAWN PLAN, for the record: the automatic stale-singleton cleanup described above is NOT what shipped. Reviewer verdict on PR 556 (2026-10-24) rejected automatic deletion because check-then-unlink cannot be made race-free and a wrong unlink can put two Chromes on one profile. Final shape, PR 556 head 4a73405f: the launcher never deletes, moves or takes over anything; it stays fail-closed and the error names the three files plus the conditions an operator must verify first - this host owns the profile, no Chrome or starting launch uses it, and if any of that is uncertain, stop.

title: Non-blocking polish for mirror trust-dialog handling (PR #440)
description:
From /advice round 7 on jleechanorg/jleechan-skills PR #440 (head e991ed42), Opus flagged two minor, explicitly non-blocking nits — both confirmed safe-fail (never a false READY), deferred rather than fixed in that PR:

1. Misleading FAILED diagnostic in the rare wrap-race case. In `.claude/skills/mac-mirror/SKILL.md` and `.claude/skills/linux-mirror/SKILL.md`, the trust-dialog accept loop verifies the cursor reached "Yes, I trust this folder" before sending Enter, but an in-flight extra Down (confirmed live: the dialog's 2-item list wraps, not clamps) can rarely land after that confirmation and flip the cursor back to "No, exit" before Enter is processed. This safely produces FAILED: (pane_dead=1), never a false READY — but the FAILED message text says "session did not survive launch (check that claude is on the remote PATH)", which misattributes the cause.
   Fix: detect this case or broaden the generic FAILED message to also mention "or the workspace-trust dialog was declined."

2. Inconsistent tmux session-name matching. has-session uses exact-match `=$SESSION`, but capture-pane/send-keys/display-message calls use the bare `$SESSION` (prefix-match). Same false-match bug class the `=` prefix was added to close.
   Fix: use `=$SESSION` (or `-t "=$SESSION"`) consistently.

Both are in `.claude/skills/mac-mirror/SKILL.md` and `.claude/skills/linux-mirror/SKILL.md`, byte-identical modulo line offsets. PR #440 merged as 9232446.

title: [P0] PR #608: Luna report writes can race past Scratch containment
description:
Provenance: jleechanorg/jleechan-skills PR #608 at exact head `d4936d5ecbf152a43f0177a6cd59b9eb18464ae6`; the Luna report-path change entered at `a6ee2469b224cc14ff941db0a7b6880041b1fff2` (verified from Git commit parents). Independent current-head code review identified an ancestor-symlink time-of-check/time-of-use gap in `.claude/skills/luna/scripts/audit_prs.py`.

P0: `get_luna_review_dir()` checks the resolved path, then creates it through the path string before its second containment check (lines 63-73). `_safe_report_path()` checks and canonicalizes by path, while `_write_report_file()` later reopens `report_path.parent` by pathname with `O_NOFOLLOW` only on the final component (lines 76-108). An ancestor such as `worldarchitect.ai` can be swapped to a symlink after validation but before `mkdir`/parent open; the operation can create the review directory or report outside configured Scratch before the later check catches it. Existing tests reject symlinks present before validation but do not exercise this race.

Acceptance to clear:
- Anchor directory creation and report writes to an already-opened Scratch root directory descriptor; walk each path component with no-follow semantics and use descriptor-relative `mkdir`/open operations, preventing ancestor replacement from redirecting writes.
- Add deterministic regression coverage that swaps an ancestor after validation and before directory creation/report open; assert no outside directory or file is created and existing outside sentinels remain unchanged.
- Keep the existing pre-existing directory/leaf symlink rejection and valid in-Scratch alias behavior passing.
- Verify the exact source head and retain the raw failure and fix receipts. No provider/browser execution is needed for this deterministic filesystem contract.

Classification: P0 merge-blocking security containment defect; this issue remains open until the race is closed and directly tested.

title: Enforce expected Dot identity before read and send
description:
## Context and provenance
The user reports logging into all three Dot accounts on both macOS and Linux nearly every day. The parent session reports that the configured Linux WorldAI slot currently authenticates as the personal account. That is a reported wrong-identity observation; the review did not receive its raw identity receipt. The review found that ordinary read/send auth handling accepts `hasUser` without comparing the configured identity, while a separate typed diagnostic probe calculates `identity_match`.

Current source snapshot: `/tmp/dot-rootcause-advice-e4bu7yfp/review/manifest.md` (captured 2026-10-10T19:17:33Z): mac `dot.sh` SHA-256 `5ac02de3cb16feca868b35b6c3bc29fa3f673592fdae9f9f3134ebc3a9c0fd08`; mac `dot_chrome.mjs` `0262ed259b6207ed36a632cc9ed26fcdd470d153372bb24b9b9f24a7a457761d`; Linux `dot.sh` `f0f54e84e72a803d8cfc32435f4d2c86c5918752e4df6c836748e803952e2d0c`; Linux `dot_chrome.mjs` `615092c8f5f67876f90ef35ef6b29dcf583b050e04d26e6b5b94018169e398b1`. The scripts were rehashed at 2026-10-10T19:21:38Z and all matched the snapshot.

The sanitized config packet emitted JSON null for absent `profile_directory` fields; presence-aware reread confirmed those fields are absent for Mac personal/test and all Linux accounts, while only Mac WorldAI explicitly sets Profile 1. This was a serialization artifact, not a live null setting; see `/tmp/dot-rootcause-advice-e4bu7yfp/config-presence-clarification.json`.

## Problem
A generic successful “signed in” response does not prove that the configured account is active. Using a different signed-in account can expose another account's data or send as the wrong identity. This is distinct from logout, cookie loss, or provider session expiry. The expected-identity code gap is confirmed; it does not explain the reported daily login prompts by itself.

## Scope
Enforce each configured account's expected identity before normal reads and sends. Resolve the correct human and automation profile for manual and scheduled launch paths as part of the mapping. On mismatch, stop before reading account data or sending, preserve the session, and return an actionable identity-mismatch result. Do not retry, sign out, refresh credentials, copy cookies, or alter auth state as remediation. Do not infer keyring/password-store failure or provider expiry without evidence.

## Acceptance criteria
- Resolve and record the intended identity and profile for every configured account/host and for manual and scheduled launch paths.
- Before each normal read and send, compare the observed identity with the slot's configured expected identity; prove mismatches stop before cross-account reads or sends.
- Add focused tests for matching identity, wrong identity, logout, and manual/scheduled mapping; show mismatch does not trigger retries, sign-out, cookie mutation, or send side effects.
- Provide safe real-service proof attributable to the exact configured profile: expected identity match and canonical read, plus a mismatch refusal before any cross-account operation. Retain only booleans and non-secret receipts.
- Keep the daily-login report as a symptom; do not claim this guard proves or fixes its cause.

## Review disposition
`/tmp/dot-rootcause-advice-e4bu7yfp/advice-synthesis.md` confirms the ordinary read/send identity gap by Codex full-coverage review. It does not validate the raw Linux wrong-account observation or establish a cause of daily prompts. Research supports possible mechanisms but not incident causality; Secondo's document-only response is not an approval; Opus was unavailable due to weekly quota. Overall advice verdict: WITHHELD. Do not use historical cookie-copy/mtime behavior, key-store hypotheses, or provider expiry as current causes without fresh evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Configured-profile identity is verified before each read/send; mismatches stop before cross-account effects; tests and safe identity proof are attributable to the exact configured profile.

title: Honor canonical comment shape in consolidated-reply idempotency
description:
Provenance: Independent full-source review of jleechanorg/jleechan-skills PR #608 at exact head `550a64f24430eb8cd21a8c974d44b7a0cac27122`, base `e2ce0e2f06864f025a97522645e7c6c645ee0041`. In `.claude/commands/_copilot_modules/commentfetch.py:174-183`, canonical issue comments are serialized as `type: "general"` with `author` populated from `user.login`. In `.claude/commands/commentreply.py:1644-1655`, the consolidated-reply idempotency check only recognizes `type` `issue`/missing and inspects `user.login`, so it does not recognize a prior response represented in the canonical `general`/`author` shape. A repeated run can therefore miss its earlier reply and post it again. This scenario is source-derived; no sender/reproduction was executed.

Acceptance:
- Make the consolidated-reply idempotency check recognize the canonical general-comment shape (`type: general`, `author`) as well as supported legacy forms.
- Add a regression proving a prior matching consolidated reply in canonical shape is skipped on rerun, while a genuinely later third-party reply remains processable.
- Verify existing legacy issue-comment shapes and actor filtering still behave as before; do not send live comments as part of the fix verification.
acceptance_criteria: Recognize a prior response in canonical type=general/author shape and skip duplicate send on rerun; continue processing genuinely later third-party replies; preserve supported legacy issue-comment handling; add focused tests without live sending.

title: Scanner attestation follow-ups from post-merge /er on PR #418
description:
Post-merge independent evidence review of jleechan-skills PR #418 (merged 3854bd1649cc) returned PARTIAL with no blocking defects and 9 follow-ups. Two are code-level and belong in a follow-up PR against jleechanorg/jleechan-skills.

D3 — empty documents bypass digest attestation. In scripts/audit_command_skill_usage.py inventory_text(), a row with content_b64 "" and content_sha256 "" is accepted, while the SAME empty document carrying its correct digest sha256(b"") = e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855 is REJECTED by the "not content and expected" branch. That inverts the intended rule and contradicts evidence.md line 129 ("bytes require a matching digest"). Not exploitable: the snapshot is hash-pinned by load_bound_json, so reaching an inconsistent row requires control of the manifest too. Fix: accept the empty document when its digest is either absent or exactly digest(b""), and reject otherwise; update the capture side to emit digest(b"") for empty content so the two halves agree; add cases for both spellings.

D7 — content_captured False short-circuits before digest validation, so a row marked uncaptured that also carries a wrong-digest payload returns "" silently instead of failing closed. Fix: validate any present content_b64 before honoring the content_captured flag, or reject a False row that carries a non-empty payload.

Both were executed and confirmed by the reviewer at the merged head, not inferred from the diff. Neither changes any current output: the real run had uncaptured_inventory_count 0 and no zero-byte, unreadable, or broken-symlink Markdown under any live inventory root.

Acceptance: a fresh failing test for each before the fix; both spellings of the empty document round-trip; capture and audit agree on the empty-document digest; full suite green with PYTHONPATH unset; no change to the 741-skill classification.

Evidence: https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/c10c1e9be281031dc6abac1cfb6b4c79 (bundle) and https://gist.github.com/jleechan2015/b00b36f2e30f44e6a7921b2b298dcb2d (parser arm).

title: npm audit: 10 advisories (1 critical) in package-lock, lockfile-only — not reachable
description:
Investigated 2026-11-01. NOT urgent; recorded so it is not re-investigated.

WHAT: npm audit in jleechan-skills reports 10 advisories (3 moderate, 6 high, 1 critical), 5 of them in prod deps. Chain: express ^4.19.2 -> body-parser/path-to-regexp/qs -> proxy-addr (critical).

WHY IT IS NOT URGENT
1. node_modules is NOT installed in the worktree. The advisories come from package-lock.json alone, so there is no live vulnerable code.
2. The only express consumer is .claude/scripts/auth-cli.mjs, a local OAuth callback server bound to 127.0.0.1 (line 547: server.listen(CONFIG.callbackPort, '127.0.0.1')). It is not a deployed or network-reachable service.
3. The critical finding (proxy-addr IP spoofing via IPv4-mapped IPv6 trust subnet) requires 'trust proxy' or req.ip handling. Grepped auth-cli.mjs: neither is used, so that advisory is unreachable here.

THE REAL FIX, WHEN WANTED
npm audit fix only touches the lockfile BUT package.json declares "prepare": "husky", and husky is a devDependency that is not installed, so any npm install in this checkout fails with:
  sh: husky: command not found  (npm error code 127)
Workaround: npm install --ignore-scripts, or install devDeps first. Do it in a worktree and commit package-lock.json explicitly; do not let it sweep unrelated changes.

NOT DONE: no lockfile change was made. Verified package.json and package-lock.json are byte-identical to before this investigation.

title: /advice is markdown-only, so the seat-parsing contract now has no executable test
description:
After #633 (delete the primary-pair runner) and #632 (markdown-only env-driven seats), /advice defines its reviewer-seat parsing ONLY as English in SKILL.md: split the env value on '|', then on the FIRST UNQUOTED '=', shlex the remainder, substitute {prompt} per occurrence, and append the request only when no occurrence exists.

Observed evidence this session: the live ~/.claude/skills/advice/SKILL.md was 81 lines stale against origin/main, and the divergence was exactly this contract - live still said 'split on the first =' while main carried the newer 'seat separation is honoured outside quotes' + '{prompt} may appear inside a token' wording. Nothing failed. There is no test that would have caught it, and no script exists to run.

Risk: two reviewers silently receive the wrong prompt because a seat spec with a quoted '=' or an inline --print={prompt} is parsed differently than documented. A prose-only contract cannot detect its own drift.

Fix direction: add a small test that pins the documented contract as executable cases (quoted '=' stays one seat; {prompt} inside a token substitutes; no occurrence appends; unparseable entry makes that seat UNAVAILABLE and never falls back). It may be a table-driven test of the documented rules rather than a restored runner - the point is that the contract has an executable pin. Wire it into contract-tests.

title: Scan split pr-lifecycle Markdown for section references
description:
Severity: P1, nonblocking test-coverage follow-up.

Context:
- PR: https://github.com/jleechanorg/jleechan-skills/pull/706
- Verified head: https://github.com/jleechanorg/jleechan-skills/commit/b3190b727c58b6f7df9a23dc57a524ad65c34da2
- Evidence: `tests/test_coding_lifecycle_contract.py` at that commit, lines 109-130; see https://github.com/jleechanorg/jleechan-skills/blob/b3190b727c58b6f7df9a23dc57a524ad65c34da2/tests/test_coding_lifecycle_contract.py#L109-L130.
- Finding: `_references()` scans `pr-lifecycle/SKILL.md` for local `§ Heading` references, then scans external `SKILL.md` files while skipping the `pr-lifecycle` package. It does not collect `§` references from the package's new `exceptions.md`, `review-records.md`, or `six-stage.md`, so a stale intra-package section reference in those on-demand files can evade this test.
- Why it matters: the test claims to protect lifecycle section references, but the split sources are now part of the same contract and can contain unchecked references. This is a coverage gap; no current broken link or runtime failure is asserted. It is nonblocking under the repository's P0-only merge-blocking policy.
- Staleness note: the method and line references were verified at head `b3190b727c58b6f7df9a23dc57a524ad65c34da2`; re-read before implementation.

Implementation:
- Files: `tests/test_coding_lifecycle_contract.py` only.
- Current API/methods: `PrLifecycleSectionReferences._headings(cls)` at lines 82-92 already reads all `pr-lifecycle/*.md`; `_references(cls)` at lines 108-131 collects references; `test_section_references_resolve(self)` calls both at lines 133-138.
- Call-site shape: keep `refs = self._references()` and compare each collected heading with `self._resolves(ref, heads)`.
- Constraints: include every Markdown file in the `pr-lifecycle` package when extracting local `§` references, keep scanning external skill files, and retain the current location labels so failures identify the originating part and line.
- Non-goals: no lifecycle policy wording changes, no production code, and no test that pins fixed Markdown phrases or ordering.
- Forbidden paths: do not add `assertIn`/`assertNotIn` phrase pins, phrase-order checks, or “old wording must not reappear” assertions; target `AGENTS.md` lines 16-23 allows only mechanical structural tests.

Acceptance criteria:
- Standards: mechanically cover all `pr-lifecycle/*.md` local references and preserve the external-skill scan.
- Static checks: `git diff --check` passes.
- Tests: `python3 -m unittest tests.test_coding_lifecycle_contract -q` passes and includes a regression demonstrating an unresolved reference from an on-demand Markdown part is reported, without pinning production wording.
- Evidence: current-head test command and output are recorded after the follow-up is implemented.
- Done when: a malformed `§` reference in any lifecycle package Markdown part is detected by the contract test; current valid references pass.

title: Non-blocking polish for mirror trust-dialog handling (PR #440)
description:
From /advice round 7 on jleechanorg/jleechan-skills PR #440 (head e991ed42), Opus flagged two minor, explicitly non-blocking nits — both confirmed safe-fail (never a false READY), deferred rather than fixed in that PR:

1. **Misleading FAILED diagnostic in the rare wrap-race case.** In `.claude/skills/mac-mirror/SKILL.md` and `linux-mirror/SKILL.md`, the trust-dialog accept loop verifies the cursor reached "Yes, I trust this folder" before sending Enter, but an in-flight extra `Down` (confirmed live: the dialog's 2-item list wraps, not clamps) can rarely land after that confirmation and flip the cursor back to "No, exit" before Enter is processed. This safely produces `FAILED:` (pane_dead=1), never a false READY — but the FAILED message text says "session did not survive launch (check that `claude` is on the remote PATH)", which misattributes the cause and would send a debugging human down the wrong first path for this specific failure mode.
   Fix: either detect this case specifically (e.g. check if the pane died with the dialog's "No, exit" path having been the last-seen state) and emit a distinct message, or broaden the generic FAILED message to also mention "or the workspace-trust dialog was declined."

2. **Inconsistent tmux session-name matching.** `has-session` uses exact-match `=$SESSION`, but the later `capture-pane`/`send-keys`/`display-message` calls in the same block use the bare `$SESSION`, which tmux prefix-matches. This is the same false-match bug class the `=` prefix was added to close (a branch whose `BRANCH_SAFE-BRANCH_HASH` is a numeric prefix of another's). Reachable only in a narrow session-name-collision edge case, but worth closing for consistency.
   Fix: use `=$SESSION` (or `-t "=$SESSION"`) for the capture-pane/send-keys/display-message calls too, matching the has-session gate.

Both are in `.claude/skills/mac-mirror/SKILL.md` and `.claude/skills/linux-mirror/SKILL.md`. Apply identically to both files (their trust-dialog blocks are byte-identical modulo line offsets, per repeated /advice review confirmation).

(Originally filed as bd-d8a on the jeff-ubuntu mirror session; recreated here after bringing that session's work back to this machine.)

title: install-claude-commands.sh: failed-install staging dirs leak into the repo working tree (5 per test run)
description:
Source: install-claude-commands.sh:331 STAGING_DIR=$(mktemp -d "${CLAUDE_HOME}.staging.XXXXXX") uses CLAUDE_HOME directly, so when it is unset or relative mktemp creates the staging dir in CWD. The failure path at :1136 then renames it to .staging.XXXXXX.failed-<ts> and keeps it 'for inspection'.

Symptom: 25 untracked .staging.*.failed-* dirs (~3.4MB, 800 md + 25 manifest.json) accumulated in the jleechan-skills worktree root; 5 were created by a fully GREEN run (942 tests OK), so this is not abort debris - every run of the installer failure-path tests pollutes the working tree.

Why it matters: (a) tests must not write into the repository tree; (b) it dirties git status for every lane using the repo, inviting accidental 'git add -A' commits; (c) the retained trees have no diagnostic value beyond regeneration - they are installer output (markdown only, no code).

Fix direction: default the staging root to a scratch/temp location when CLAUDE_HOME is unset or not absolute (fail closed rather than writing to CWD), keep the .failed- renames inside that root, and have the failure-path test assert the rename stays under its temp dir. Verify by running the suite twice and confirming git status is clean and zero .staging dirs remain in CWD.

title: Separate hyphenated split feature names from series prefixes
description:
Provenance: PRW-716 read-only review of PR #506 at published head `023da1dfe8018f25901bbfaf7f32ad8cb0d05a5e`; reproduced locally on the current PR candidate. Owner: `.claude/hooks/protect-pr-create.sh` and the split naming contract in `.claude/skills/pr-quantity-control/SKILL.md`.

Finding (P2, nonblocking): `compute_split_prefix` treats a hyphen in a feature name as a series delimiter. With five open heads named `split/auth-other/*`, `gh pr create --head split/auth-login --base main` is blocked because the calculated prefix is `split/auth-`. A hyphenated feature name and a split-series suffix are ambiguous under the current naming rule.

Reproduction: the local hook test stub supplies five `split/auth-other/<n>` open PRs; the command above returns exit 2 with `split PR quantity cap exceeded`.

Acceptance: clarify the supported delimiter in the owning policy and align the hook so unrelated hyphenated feature names do not share a prefix. Preserve the existing cap values; add deterministic allow/block coverage for both the split delimiter and ordinary hyphenated feature names.

title: Verify Linux Dot profile mapping and launcher parity
description:
## Context and provenance
The user reports logging into all three Dot accounts on both macOS and Linux nearly every day. The parent session reports that the configured Linux WorldAI slot currently authenticates as the personal account, but the review did not receive its raw identity receipt.

Current source snapshot: `/tmp/dot-rootcause-advice-e4bu7yfp/review/manifest.md` (captured 2026-10-10T19:17:33Z): mac `dot.sh` SHA-256 `5ac02de3cb16feca868b35b6c3bc29fa3f673592fdae9f9f3134ebc3a9c0fd08`; mac `dot_chrome.mjs` `0262ed259b6207ed36a632cc9ed26fcdd470d153372bb24b9b9f24a7a457761d`; Linux `dot.sh` `f0f54e84e72a803d8cfc32435f4d2c86c5918752e4df6c836748e803952e2d0c`; Linux `dot_chrome.mjs` `615092c8f5f67876f90ef35ef6b29dcf583b050e04d26e6b5b94018169e398b1`. All four installed scripts were rehashed at 2026-10-10T19:21:38Z and matched this snapshot.

The review confirms installed launcher drift: Linux lacks Mac's `profile_directory` wiring, and all Linux config entries omit that field. The presence-aware config reread found the field absent for Mac personal/test and every Linux account; only Mac WorldAI explicitly sets Profile 1. The earlier JSON nulls were a serialization artifact. Different subprofile names across hosts are not inherently a defect; if the intended Linux session is already in `Default`, the missing option cannot explain a wrong identity.

## Scope
Verify and, if required, promote Linux launcher support for explicit `profile_directory` so account/profile selection is attributable and consistent across manual and scheduled launches. Identify the intended human and automation profile for each configured account. Treat launcher drift as a capability gap, not a proven cause of the reported daily prompts. Preserve existing sessions; never copy Chrome cookies or profiles between hosts/accounts. Do not infer keyring/password-store or provider-expiry remediation without evidence.

## Acceptance criteria
- Map all three configured account slots to host, executable, user-data root, Chrome subprofile, expected identity, and manual/scheduled launcher.
- Prove startup on the configured Linux target honors the intended profile selection and yields the expected identity plus a canonical read; document any legitimate Mac/Linux profile-name difference.
- Add focused startup/profile-selection coverage if code changes are needed, then prove installed source parity at the exact tested version.
- Do not claim that Linux's `Default` selection caused a wrong identity or daily login prompts without a reproduction linking profile selection to that outcome.
- Preserve sessions and avoid cookie copying, sign-outs, retries, or auth repair during investigation.

## Review disposition
`/tmp/dot-rootcause-advice-e4bu7yfp/advice-synthesis.md` confirms Linux launcher drift but no causal Linux proof. Research supports possible mechanisms, not incident attribution; Secondo's document-only response is not an approval; Opus was unavailable due to weekly quota. Overall advice verdict: WITHHELD. Historical cookie-copy/mtime behavior is retired and absent from both installed source snapshots.
acceptance_criteria: Manual and scheduled launches are mapped to the intended account/profile on both hosts; Linux profile selection and canonical read are proved on the configured target; no causal claim or auth repair without evidence.

title: Live ~/.claude/skills copies drift from the repo silently; no automated drift detection
description:
Two live-vs-repo drifts were found this session, both by accident, both material:

1. ~/.claude/skills/roadmap/SKILL.md was AHEAD of origin/main by 26 diff lines (private-repo profile guidance, the 'keep the tab on the GitHub URL' clause, TLDR timestamp wording). Discovered only because a board run happened to diff the two copies.
2. ~/.claude/skills/advice/SKILL.md was 81 lines BEHIND main, and the stale span was the reviewer-seat parsing contract.

There is no check that compares the live skill root against jleechan-skills origin/main. The skills that matter most (advice, roadmap, pr-lifecycle, cmux-bulk-steer) are the ones most likely to be edited live under time pressure.

Direction is now documented as one-way repo -> live in .claude/skills/roadmap/SKILL.md (landed in #646), but documenting the direction does not detect a violation.

Fix direction: a read-only checker script under scripts/ that, for each skill present in both roots, prints skills whose live SKILL.md differs from origin/main, with a unified diff and an exit code usable in CI or a launchd/cron report.
